title: Janakpur Pilgrimage Guide: Temples, Aarti and Festivals
meta_description: Janakpur pilgrimage guide: Janaki Mandir darshan and aarti, Vivah Mandap, Ram Mandir, sacred ponds, Dhanusadham, festivals, how to reach and where to stay.
summary: Janakpur, believed to be Sita's birthplace, is best visited over two nights: darshan and evening aarti at the Janaki Mandir, the Vivah Mandap, the Ram Mandir and Ganga Sagar, plus a half day at Dhanusadham. Fly from Kathmandu in 25 minutes or come from Jaynagar in Bihar. October to March is most comfortable.

sections.heading: Why Janakpur matters to pilgrims
paras: In the Ramayana, King Janak of Mithila found the infant Sita in a furrow while ploughing a field, raised her as his daughter, and later held the swayamvara at which Rama broke Shiva's bow and won her hand. Janakpur, or Janakpurdham, is identified with Janak's capital. For Hindu pilgrims, especially from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and the Nepali Terai, a visit here balances Ayodhya, Rama's birthplace: one is the groom's city, the other the bride's.

The city today is busy and dusty, but its religious life is intense. Pilgrims bathe in sacred ponds at dawn, crowd the Janaki Mandir for the evening aarti, and sing Sita–Ram bhajans in Maithili and Hindi. Janakpur is also the cultural heart of Mithila, home of the bold Mithila painting tradition, which gives the pilgrimage a distinctive local flavour.

sections.heading: The main temples and sacred sites
paras: Most of Janakpur's important shrines lie within about 2 km of each other, so a well-planned day covers them on foot or by e-rickshaw. The table lists the sites we include on our Janakpur tours, with typical visit times.

sections.heading: Janaki Mandir darshan and aarti
paras: The Janaki Mandir was built by Queen Vrisha Bhanu of Tikamgarh and completed in 1910. Its three storeys of white stone and marble, domes and 60 rooms recall a Rajput palace, and locals call it the Naulakha Mandir after its reputed cost of nine lakh rupees. The sanctum holds images of Sita, Rama and his brothers. Rooms around the courtyard house a museum of Mithila art and Ramayana scenes.

The temple generally opens early in the morning, closes for a period around midday and reopens in the afternoon until after the evening aarti, around 8 to 9 pm; hours vary by season and festival, so check current status before you travel. The evening aarti at sunset is the high point of any visit, with tiered lamps, bells, conch shells and the crowd singing. Arrive 30 minutes early to find space in the courtyard, and come back for a quieter morning darshan.

sections.heading: Festivals worth planning around
paras: Janakpur celebrates many Hindu festivals, but a few transform the city. Each brings crowds, higher hotel prices and the need to book early.
list: Vivah Panchami (Nov–Dec): re-enactment of Sita and Rama's wedding, with processions from Ayodhya; 14 December in 2026
Ram Navami (Mar–Apr): Rama's birthday, centred on the Ram Mandir
Sita Navami or Janaki Navami (Apr–May): Sita's appearance day at the Janaki Mandir
Chhath (Oct–Nov, after Diwali): sunset and sunrise offerings to the sun god at the ponds, a huge Mithila festival
Makar Sankranti (mid-January): fair at Dhanusadham and ritual bathing
Parikrama in Phagun (Feb–Mar): pilgrims walk the circuit around Janakpur's sacred sites

sections.heading: How to reach Janakpur
paras: From Kathmandu, the quickest way is a 25-minute flight with Buddha Air or Shree Airlines to Janakpur Airport, 2 km from the temple. By road it is about 230 km and 7–8 hours via the BP Highway through Sindhuli and Bardibas. From Chitwan, it is about 280 km and 7–8 hours east along the Mahendra Highway via Hetauda.

From India, Indian pilgrims usually cross at Jaynagar in Bihar, about 30 km away, by the cross-border train to Janakpur or by road. Raxaul–Birgunj is about 4–5 hours by road. Sitamarhi, with Punaura Dham believed to be Sita's birthplace on the Indian side, is about 50 km away, and many groups combine the two. Indian citizens need a passport or voter ID card.

sections.heading: Where to stay and what to eat
paras: Janakpur's hotels are simple, mostly 2- to 3-star, with clean rooms, air conditioning in better rooms, and pure vegetarian kitchens. Choose one within walking distance of the Janaki Mandir, because roads close to vehicles during festivals and walking to the evening aarti is part of the experience. During Vivah Panchami and Ram Navami rooms sell out weeks ahead.

Food around the temples is vegetarian: dal-bhat, puri-sabzi, kachori, litti-chokha, and Maithili sweets such as peda, jalebi, malpua and the curd-based dahi of Mithila. Hotels serve North Indian thalis, and Jain meals can be arranged. Drink bottled or filtered water and choose busy stalls for street snacks.

sections.heading: Practical tips for pilgrims
paras: A little preparation makes Janakpur far more comfortable, especially for families and older pilgrims.
list: Visit from October to March; April to June often passes 40 °C
Pack a warm shawl in December and January for foggy, cold evenings near 7–10 °C
Dress modestly, leave leather at the hotel and use the free shoe stand at the temple gate
Keep small notes for offerings, prasad and donation boxes
Use e-rickshaws for short hops; lanes are busy with motorbikes
Agree a meeting point with your group at the Janaki Mandir, especially during festivals

faqs.q: Is Janakpur the birthplace of Sita?
faqs.a: Hindu tradition identifies Janakpur with the capital of King Janak, Sita's father, and the place where she was found and raised. Sitamarhi in Bihar, about 50 km away, also claims to be the spot where she appeared. Many pilgrims visit both. Janakpur is also believed to be where Sita and Rama married.

faqs.q: How many days are needed for a Janakpur pilgrimage?
faqs.a: Two nights is ideal: one full day for the Janaki Mandir, Vivah Mandap, Ram Mandir, ponds and aarti, and a half day for Dhanusadham and the Mithila art centre. One night is possible with a flight. For Vivah Panchami, plan three nights.

faqs.q: What is the Janaki Mandir aarti time?
faqs.a: The evening aarti is at sunset, roughly 5:30 pm in winter and 7 pm in summer, with a morning aarti soon after opening. Exact times vary with season and festivals. Arrive half an hour early to find space in the courtyard, and check with your guide on the day.

faqs.q: How do I reach Janakpur from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: By a 25-minute flight with Buddha Air or Shree Airlines, or by road in 7–8 hours via the BP Highway through Sindhuli and Bardibas, about 230 km. Buses also run day and night. Flying one way and driving the other is a good compromise.

faqs.q: How do I reach Janakpur from Bihar?
faqs.a: From Jaynagar, about 30 km away, by the cross-border train to Janakpur or by road in about an hour. From Sitamarhi, it is about 50 km and 2 hours via Bhitthamore. Indian citizens need a passport or voter ID. Third-country nationals should use an international border such as Raxaul–Birgunj.

faqs.q: When is Vivah Panchami in Janakpur?
faqs.a: Vivah Panchami falls on the fifth day of the bright half of Mangsir, in late November or December. In 2026 most published calendars give 14 December. Celebrations run for about a week before. Book hotels and flights at least two months ahead.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Janakpur?
faqs.a: October to March, when days are 18–28 °C. Vivah Panchami, Chhath and Ram Navami are the big festival periods. April to June is very hot, often above 40 °C, and July to September is monsoon, with heavy rain and occasional flooding.

faqs.q: Are there good hotels in Janakpur?
faqs.a: Janakpur's hotels are simple 2- to 3-star properties with clean rooms and vegetarian food, not resorts. The best options are within walking distance of the Janaki Mandir. We choose hotels for location and cleanliness and book them early for festival dates.

faqs.q: Can I combine Janakpur with other pilgrimages in Nepal?
faqs.a: Yes. Our Devghat and Janakpur yatra links Pashupatinath, Manakamana, Devghat and Janakpur in six days. Many pilgrims also combine Janakpur with Muktinath via Pokhara, or with Lumbini on a wider Nepal pilgrimage. Indian groups often add Sitamarhi.
